world.bio: I'm Callum, forty-three, an Australian surfboard shaper from the Gold Coast who moved to Portugal eight years ago with my wife Inês and our daughter. I shape about a hundred and fifty boards a year in a garage workshop in Ericeira, mostly for local surfers and a few clients in the Algarve and Biarritz. I love the smell of fresh foam and I know every curve of a good rocker. I've also started coughing at night, which I'm pretending is nothing. I rebuild a VW van engine on the side and teach my daughter to surf at dawn.
skills_assets: Hand-shapes about 150 custom surfboards a year in a garage workshop in Ericeira
Twenty years of shaping experience: shortboards, mid-lengths, fish and a few guns
A workshop with a planer, sanding blocks, a dust extraction unit, a glassing bay and a small spray booth
Regular clients among Ericeira locals, plus repeat orders from a surf school and two shops in Peniche and Lagos
A stock of EPS and PU blanks, fibreglass cloth, epoxy and polyester resins
A 1978 VW van he is rebuilding
Portuguese residency card (due for renewal) and a small business registration as a sole trader

projects.name: Custom board orders
projects.text: Orders run about three to four weeks. Autumn is busy because swell season starts. I am shaping eleven boards right now: three fish, four mid-lengths, two guns for a Nazaré client, two groms' boards. The work is physical and slow, and I'm proud of it, but the glassing and laminating stages leave me with a chest that burns by evening.

projects.name: Resin alternatives
projects.text: I have been reading about bio-resins: plant-based epoxies, flax fibre, cork. The commercial ones I tried yellow too fast in the sun, and surfers hate a yellow board. I want something that lasts three seasons without turning the colour of weak tea. No supplier I've found has convinced me.

projects.name: VW van rebuild
projects.text: 1978 Type 2, engine apart on my workshop bench. It's my break from foam dust. Inês says it is a very expensive way to avoid doctors.

notes.text: Cough again last night, woke Inês. She asked if I wanted water. I said no, it passes. It didn't pass for forty minutes. I sat on the back step in my shorts watching the Atlantic go from black to grey. Am I imagining that it's worse after a laminating day?

Taught Matilde to duck-dive today. She's nine and fearless and has no idea how much I rely on her not noticing me cough. We ate pastéis de nata on the wall afterwards. She said, Pai, you sound like Vovô. I laughed. I did not like it.

Went to the GP. He listened to my chest for a long time, asked about my work, resin, isocyanates, the spray booth. Said it is likely from fumes and he wants me to cut exposure. I said, I make boards, how do I cut exposure? He said, that's your problem to solve, and gave me a referral for a lung function test.

Told Inês the GP's verdict. She went quiet, then said we'll figure it out. She didn't say it with certainty. I walked to the workshop and stood in the middle of the floor, hands in pockets, not touching anything.
Ordered a better respirator, one with cartridges for organic vapours. €142. Told myself it solves the problem. It doesn't. It only solves the part that I can see.

Clients are asking about lead times for December. I said six weeks. I know I can't do six weeks with a half-working chest. I should hire help, but hire who? Everyone I know who can glass a board properly has their own shop.

Read a forum post by a shaper in Santa Cruz who switched to a bio-based resin and said it cut his cough. Other comments said it yellowed, cracked, delaminated. I don't know who to believe. I'm tired of reading and not knowing.
Residency renewal appointment at AIMA moved to November. Third reschedule. Inês keeps saying it will be fine. I keep thinking: if my lungs go and my papers lapse, what exactly am I doing here?
Spent the afternoon with the VW engine. Cleaned the carburettor, no cough at all. Maybe it's the wrong kind of dust, the right kind of dust. Maybe it's just the foam. Maybe I'm kidding myself.

messages.text:
Inês: Did you take your tablets?
Me: Which tablets?
Inês: The ones for the cough, Callum.
Me: Right. Yes.

Rui: Callum, I need six boards by December for the school.
Me: Six weeks, maybe seven.
Rui: Can't you do five?
Me: I'll see what I can do. Don't hold me to it.

Lachlan: Heard you got a diagnosis?
Me: Not a diagnosis. Warning.
Lachlan: Mate, hang up the planer for a while.
Me: And do what, exactly?

Bruno: New epoxy arrives Tuesday. Same price.
Me: Is there anything without isocyanates?
Bruno: Not that surfers will accept.
Me: Right.

Matilde: Pai, can we surf at six tomorrow?
Me: Yes. Bring your wetsuit.
Matilde: And you promise you won't cough?
Me: I promise I'll try.

relations.about: Surf school client, wants six boards by December.
Resin supplier, honest about the limits of bio-based options.
Old mate on the Gold Coast.

constraints: Cannot cut output below about 100 boards a year without hurting income
Will not use a resin that yellows fast
Will not hire anyone he doesn't trust with glassing
sensitive: His GP told him in September that the night cough is likely from resin and isocyanate fumes and asked him to cut exposure
Fear of losing the ability to shape
Money worries if he cuts production
